setlist_extra.title: Stuck Inside Of Mobile With The Memphis Blues Again

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Loose Lucy** (4 reviews, 4 other sources): Reviewer says this performance still gives them chills; Played for the first time in ages on the 14th, a rarity of the run [1][2][3][4][16][17][18][22]
- **Let It Grow** (4 reviews, 1 other source): Reviewer is certain this first-set closer is the version released on Without A Net in 1990; Reviewer says this is definitely the version that appears on Without A Net [1][19][20][21][23]
- **Good Time Blues** (1 review): Brent sings an excellent version, according to the reviewer [22]
- **Big River** (1 review): Brent's piano playing is singled out as especially hot [22]

## Setlist highlights

- **Loose Lucy**: back after 260 archived shows (1184 days) [26]
- **Memphis Blues Again**: rare: 13 archived performances [26]

## The recordings

- **gd1990-03-14.mtx.tobin.89693.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 152 min; rated 4.64/5 by 11 [1]
- **gd90-03-14.sbd.ladner.8466.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 154 min; rated 4.14/5 by 28 [2]. Said about its sound: MIDI work is nice throughout; some hiss between songs, but it fades once the music starts [21]
- **gd1990-03-14.140959.sbd.miller.flac2496**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 155 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [3]
- **gd1990-03-14.140969.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac1644**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 155 min [4]

## Around the show

- Reviewer's first Dead show, attended as a high school student; Blue Unicorns were obtained in the parking lot [14]
- Show fell the night before Phil's 50th birthday; reviewer attended all three Capital Centre nights [16]
- Camping and vending had been lost, yet the scene was packed to bursting; this followed the Warlocks fall tour [18]
- It was the reviewer's first Dead show, and Let It Grow left a strong impression [19]
- Opening night of the 1990 East Coast run; the reviewer feels it has been overlooked [20]
- Reviewer listened from outside by a service door while people climbed onto the roof and entered through ductwork [24]
- Mounted patrol arrived and began beating people outside the arena [24]
- The 15th is called the highlight; the 16th was more laid back than the first two high-energy nights [16]
- Reviewer thinks the band hit its stride earlier, in 1989 at Frost and Alpine, with great confidence [20]
- Reviewer knows of no better run in ten years, apart from the Warlocks 89 shows [21]
- First set is strong, but the second set is unremarkable and many better shows exist [23]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1990-03-14.mtx.tobin.89693.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Kevin Tobin; source: SBD + AUD Matrix 2 Source Mix (60%-SBD/40%-AUD) [1]. Also: Video-sourced master: JVC single-tube camera with Nak 300 shotgun mics, recorded to S-VHS, then transferred through multiple generations [1]
- **gd90-03-14.sbd.ladner.8466.sbeok.shnf**: source: sbd>mc>dats>Soundforge 4.5>CD [2]. Also: The band recorded shows for a live album, with John Cutler supervising; reviewer guesses multitrack analog reels, 24 or 48 track; Soundboard to cassette to DAT, then Soundforge 4.5 to CD, via Tom E; hosted at candyman.etree.org [2][19]
- **gd1990-03-14.140959.sbd.miller.flac2496**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Ultra Matrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-X90) [3]. Also: Two sets of masters were combined to make the show complete [3]
- **gd1990-03-14.140969.UltraMatrix.sbd.cm.miller.flac1644**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Ultra Matrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-X90) [4]. Also: UltraMatrix soundboard mix; two sets of masters were used for completeness; this file set is 16 bit [4]
- Recording info lists an UltraMatrix soundboard source going to a cassette master [31]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Dave Goodwich: [30th Anniversary of The Grateful Dead's Spring 1990 Tour: The Capital Centre, Landover, MD 3/15/90 - Glide Magazine](https://glidemagazine.com/241497/30th-anniversary-of-grateful-deads-spring-1990-tour-3-15-90-the-capital-centre-landover-md/) [28]
- Poster by Dave Goodwich: [30th Anniversary of The Grateful Dead's Spring 1990 Tour: The Capital Centre, Landover, MD 3/16/90 - Glide Magazine](https://glidemagazine.com/241539/30th-anniversary-of-grateful-deads-spring-1990-tour-3-16-90-the-capital-centre-landover-md/) [29]
- Fan art by keyboardpiano: [Grateful Dead Terrapin Station Spring 1990 Capital Centre](https://www.keyboardpiano.org/products/grateful-dead-terrapin-station-spring-1990-capital.html) [30]

citations.title: Glide Magazine: The 30th Anniversary of GD Spring 90 (the series)

claims.text: Reviewer's first Dead show, attended as a high school student; Blue Unicorns were obtained in the parking lot
Show fell the night before Phil's 50th birthday; reviewer attended all three Capital Centre nights
The 15th is called the highlight; the 16th was more laid back than the first two high-energy nights
Reviewer says this performance still gives them chills
Played for the first time in ages on the 14th, a rarity of the run
Singled out as the high point of the night
Camping and vending had been lost, yet the scene was packed to bursting; this followed the Warlocks fall tour
The band recorded shows for a live album, with John Cutler supervising; reviewer guesses multitrack analog reels, 24 or 48 track
Reviewer is certain this first-set closer is the version released on Without A Net in 1990
It was the reviewer's first Dead show, and Let It Grow left a strong impression
Opening night of the 1990 East Coast run; the reviewer feels it has been overlooked
Reviewer thinks the band hit its stride earlier, in 1989 at Frost and Alpine, with great confidence
Reviewer says this is definitely the version that appears on Without A Net
Reviewer knows of no better run in ten years, apart from the Warlocks 89 shows
Appears on Without a Net, which the reviewer thinks is well deserved
MIDI work is nice throughout; some hiss between songs, but it fades once the music starts
Brent sings an excellent version, according to the reviewer
Brent's piano playing is singled out as especially hot
Reviewer found it a great surprise in the first set
First set is strong, but the second set is unremarkable and many better shows exist
Named, along with Loose Lucy, as a highlight of the show
Reviewer listened from outside by a service door while people climbed onto the roof and entered through ductwork
Mounted patrol arrived and began beating people outside the arena
First played since 10/19/74; the crowd noise in the background is intense
Video-sourced master: JVC single-tube camera with Nak 300 shotgun mics, recorded to S-VHS, then transferred through multiple generations
Uploader is nearly certain this version is the one on Without A Net
Uploader notes it was the first performance since 10/19/74
Soundboard to cassette to DAT, then Soundforge 4.5 to CD, via Tom E; hosted at candyman.etree.org
Uploader notes it was the first one since October 19, 1974
Two sets of masters were combined to make the show complete
Uploader notes it was the first one since October 19, 1974
UltraMatrix soundboard mix; two sets of masters were used for completeness; this file set is 16 bit
Recording info lists an UltraMatrix soundboard source going to a cassette master
